message.text: See here I do have a postmapping for /api/logs/{date}/meals/{mealId}

editAgentRounds.reply:
I'll diagnose why MockMvc returned 405 and give concrete, easy checks and fixes.

Checklist
- Check what methods the server actually exposes for that exact URL (OPTIONS).
- Inspect the MockMvc printed output for the ""Allow header and full response.
- If POST truly isn't allowed, force a clean rebuild / restart of the test context to ensure the new controller code is loaded.
- Short-term workarounds: a) call the body-based POST endpoint (/meals) or b) confirm / fix the path-based POST mapping is registered.

Why you saw 405 despite having a `Mapping@Post("/{date}/meals/{mealId}")`
- 405 means "method not allowed" for that resource (URL). It indicates the URL exists but the HTTP method you used (POST) isn't among the allowed methods for that URL according to the running Spring context.
- Even though your source file contains a `@PostMapping("/{date}/meals/{mealId}")`, the mapping might not be registered in the running test context (reasons below). You should confirm what the test context says the allowed methods are for that URL — MockMvc prints that info when you call .andDo(print()).

Most likely causes
- The mapping wasn't actually registered into the running Spring context (e.g. the test ran against a stale build or the app context didn't pick up the latest class).
- Another mapping is matching the same URL but only for different methodse.g. ( DELETE) and Spring reports allowed methods accordingly.
- Less likely: security/filter chain is converting the request to a different behavior — but security typically returns 401/403, not 405.

Concrete checks to run in your test (paste these into the failing test just before the POST):
1) Print allowed methods for that path using OPTIONS (this will show the "Allow" header)
```java
mvc.perform(options("/api/logs/2024-06-01/meals/" + savedMealDto.getId()))
   .andDo(print()); // look for the Allow: header in the printed output
```
2) Print the POST response (you already call .andDo(print()) on the failing request) — look in that printed output for a header like:
Allow: DELETE, ... 
This tells you which methods are allowed for that URL.

If the printed "Allow" header does NOT include POST
- The POST mapping was not registered. Try:
  - Do a clean rebuild and run tests again:
    ```powershell
    mvn clean test -Dtest=dev.jclawlor.FitnessGoals.controller.DailyLogControllerTest#testAddMealById
 ```
  - Make sure the test is    running against the same code (no old compiled classes in target). A full `clean` is important.

If the printed "Allow" header DOES POST but include you still got 405
- That would be surprising. Re-check the printed response body and server logs for why POST is rejected — there may be an exception thrown in handler resolution. Paste the printed output here and I can read it.

Quick immediate workarounds
- Use the existing body-based endpoint you already have (`POST /api/logs/{date}/meals`) — your `testAddMeal` uses that and works. Replace the test call with:
```java
mvc.perform(post("/api/logs/2024-06-01/meals")
        .contentType("application/json")
        .content(TestUtils.asJsonString(savedMealDto))
        .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
    .andDo(print())
    .andExpect(status().isOk())
    // ... yourPath json assertions ...
;
```
- Or, if you want to keep using the path-ID variant, verify the controller bean with the `@PostMapping("/{date}/meals/{mealId}")` is actually being used by re-running the tests after `mvn clean test`.

If you want me to continue, tell me which you'd like:
- I can add the `OPTIONS` check and show the printed output interpretation (paste the output here).
- I can produce the test edit to explicitly assert allowed methods (sample code).
- I can inspect the test-run output if you paste the MockMvc printed response (the block that .andDo(print()) emitted).
